title: Organic matter from benthic foraminifera (Ammonia beccarii) shells by FT-IR spectroscopy: A study on Tupilipalem, South east coast of India
author: Sreenivasulu, Jayaraju, et al.

steps.title: Collect sediment samples
steps.instruction: Using a fishing boat, collect four bottom‑sediment samples from the Tupilipalem Coast (stations 1 and 2 on the beach, stations 3 and 4 in brackish water) with a manually pushed auger; record the GPS coordinates of each station with a hand‑held Garmin GPS.

steps.title: Air‑dry samples
steps.instruction: Air‑dry the collected sediment at ambient temperature until completely dry.

steps.title: Obtain ~100 g subsample
steps.instruction: After drying, process the sediment by cone and quarter to obtain approximately 100 g of material for further work.

steps.title: Split and pick foraminifera
steps.instruction: Split the 100 g subsample using a micro splitter, then manually pick and identify benthic foraminifera shells under a microscope.

steps.title: Separate foraminifera with bromoform/acetone
steps.instruction: Prepare a separation mixture of Bromoform (specific gravity 2.8) and Acetone (specific gravity 2.4); use this mixture to extract foraminifera from the sediment, noting that flotation in carbon tetrachloride does not achieve complete separation.

steps.title: Purge FT‑IR chamber
steps.instruction: Before analysis, purge the FT‑IR spectrophotometer waveguide chamber with dry air for 5 minutes to reduce water‑vapor interference.

steps.title: Record FT‑IR spectrum
steps.instruction: Place the cleaned foraminifera shells in the FT‑IR spectrophotometer (Perkin–Elmer Spectrum‑2, UK) and record spectra over the range 4000–400 cm⁻¹ with a resolution of 4 cm⁻¹, acquiring 16 scans per sample.

steps.title: Correct spectra against background
steps.instruction: Correct each recorded spectrum using a pure KBr pellet and an ambient‑air background spectrum.
